subject: history_social
passage: The earliest Roman calendar began the year in March. Its seventh month was called September, from septem, the Latin word for "seven." Later, two months, January and February, were added, and the year eventually came to begin in January. ______ September became the ninth month, even though its name still means "seven."
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The text explains that two months were added and the year came to start in January. That change moved September from seventh place to ninth. The last sentence is the effect of that change, so a cause-and-effect transition is needed. (In American English the period goes inside the closing quotation mark.)
explanation.A: Incorrect. September becoming the ninth month is not an example of the calendar change; it is what the change caused.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The last sentence does not oppose the earlier ones; it follows from them. The "even though" in that sentence may make a contrast word tempting.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a parallel idea, but the last sentence states a consequence.
explanation.D: Correct. "As a result" shows that September became the ninth month because January and February came to start the year.
